JTI Profile Cleansing KPI User Guide

Go Live Date: 1st September 2026

A reference for the JTI Profile Cleansing KPI user guide and data quality KPI framework - covering dashboard purpose, system architecture, KPI definitions, calculation logic, market scope, and implementation notes across 28 markets.

▮

Purpose of the Power BI Dashboard

This KPI dashboard is aimed to act as a central monitoring tool for JTI's data quality and profile cleansing programme. It consolidates KPI results across all 28 active markets and multiple data quality dimensions into a single, interactive view - updated on a monthly cadence.

📈 Month-by-Month Progress Tracking

Each KPI is trended over time so business stakeholders can see whether data quality is improving, stagnating, or deteriorating market by market. Trend lines expose the velocity of improvement following a cleansing sprint.

🌎 Market-Level Visibility

Results are broken down by market code, enabling regional teams and the central DQ team to identify outlier markets, prioritise remediation efforts, and compare performance across geographies without manual data pulls.

📋 Business Planning Support

By surfacing contactability rates, duplicate volumes, and consent integration gaps, the dashboard feeds directly into marketing campaign planning — helping the business understand the effective reachable audience and avoid wasted spend on low-quality profiles.

✅ Cleansing Action Validation

After a cleansing action is executed (e.g. orphan profile removal or phone number correction), the dashboard confirms whether the next monthly run reflects the expected improvement — closing the loop between DQ engineering and business outcome.

Why This Is Done

Profile cleansing is not a one-off exercise — it is a continuous quality gate that protects the integrity of every downstream marketing and analytics action JTI takes on Ploom consumer data.

📱

Protect Contactability

Invalid or duplicate phone numbers and emails mean marketing messages never reach real consumers. Contactability KPIs ensure the reachable base is accurately known before campaign sizing.

💰

Reduce Wasted Spend

Test profiles and orphan profiles inflate the apparent audience size. Removing them prevents budget being allocated to unreachable or invalid profiles.

⚖

Regulatory & Consent Compliance

The consent integration KPI ensures that OneTrust consent records are fully reflected in CDP. Gaps mean messages could be sent to consumers who have not opted in — a legal risk.

📈

Data-Driven Decision Making

Clean, trusted data enables reliable segmentation, accurate campaign performance attribution, and confident business planning across all active markets.

📋

Data Quality KPIs

JTI is moving every market to a new Global Data Model (GDM). Each market has its own GDM cut-off date: until that date it is measured with the Old GDM KPIs, and from that date with the New GDM KPIs. See Implementation Notes for the markets migrated so far.

Duplicate Profiles

Profiles with the same email, phone, or legacy system identifier are treated as duplicates and must be curated to ensure a clean, single-view consumer record.

UnitPercentage
FrequencyMonthly
Primary Databasedb_l1_harmonization_[mkt]
Data LayerL1 Harmonization

What the query does

Scans matching identity keys (email, phone, legacy system) and flags profiles that appear more than once in the same profile estate. Duplicates across different legacy systems are also captured.

Result fields

  • profile.id_profile
  • profile.phone
  • profile.email
  • profile.legacy_system
Formula: (Duplicate Profile Count ÷ Total Profiles) × 100
  1. 1Group all profiles by identity key — email, phone, or legacy_system — and count occurrences per group.
  2. 2Flag every profile where any identity key count > 1 as a duplicate (all members of a duplicate group are counted).
  3. 3Sum flagged profile.id_profile values → Numerator.
  4. 4Count all distinct profile.id_profile in the estate → Denominator.
  5. 5Compute: (Numerator ÷ Denominator) × 100 = % duplicate profiles.
Cross-system duplicates (same key across different legacy systems) are also captured in this logic.
NumeratorProfiles identified as duplicates (profile.id_profile)
DenominatorTotal profiles in estate (profile.id_profile)
UnitPercentage
FrequencyMonthly
Primary DBdb_l1_harmonization_[mkt]
Data LayerL1 Harmonization
Key Fields
profile.id_profile profile.phone profile.email profile.legacy_system
Prepared for the JTI Profile Cleansing KPI Project  •  Version 1.1

Potential Invalid Phone Format

Phone numbers missing a valid country code, of incorrect length, or failing market-specific routing rules — indicating the profile cannot be reached via SMS or voice channels.

UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Primary Databasedb_l1_harmonization_[mkt]
Supporting Databasedb_technical_[mkt]

What the query does

Checks each profile's phone number against the expected format for its market — validating country code prefix, total length, and length without prefix. Where a market has additional routing rules, those are applied on top of the base check.

Result fields

  • profile.id_profile
  • profile.phone
  • profile.email
Formula: Count of profiles with an invalid phone number
  1. 1Filter to profiles where profile.phone is not null — only these are checked.
  2. 2For each profile, validate the phone number against its market rule: check country code prefix, total digit length, and length without prefix.
  3. 3Profiles failing validation are flagged as invalid — phone_validity.is_contactable = false.
  4. 4Count the flagged profiles → KPI value (number of profiles with an invalid phone format).
Validation rule per market: country code prefix + total phone length + length without prefix. Market-specific overrides apply on top.
MeasureProfiles with an invalid phone number
ScopeProfiles with a phone field populated
UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Primary DBdb_l1_harmonization_[mkt]
Supporting DBdb_technical_[mkt]
Key Fields
profile.id_profile profile.phone phone_validity.is_contactable profile.email

Test Profiles

Test, internal or dummy profiles that are still live in CDP (L1) and confirmed active in their source system (EVO) — identified through email, name and acquisition-source patterns. These are non-customer profiles and must be excluded from consumer reporting and campaign targeting.

UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Primary Databasedb_l1_harmonization_[mkt]
Supporting SourceEVO extracts (CAS, OLA, SNP)

What the query does

Builds the set of in-scope CDP profiles per legacy source system, keeping only profiles that still exist in EVO (or, for direct ingestion, exist in no other system). It then flags a profile as a test profile if its email, first/last name or acquisition source matches a test pattern, after removing a per-market list of known accounts. Results are stored per market and report month.

Result fields

  • uuid — CDP profile ID
  • source — legacy system (CAS, OLA, SNP, Ambassador, One to One)
  • probable_first_name_last_name_test — Y if first or last name contains "test"
  • probable_test_JTI_account — Y if the email is a JTI address
  • inbucket_users — Y if the email is an inbucket test-mailbox address
  • date_created_ts — profile creation date
  • market, report_month, report_run_ts
KPI value = Count of distinct profiles flagged as test profiles
  1. 1Load CDP profiles from db_l1_harmonization_[mkt].profile and the EVO extracts for the market (CAS consumers, OLA leads, SNP marketing communications).
  2. 2Build the in-scope population by source system, keeping only EVO records whose email is not anonymised:
    • CAS — profile ID exists in EVO CAS consumers.
    • OLA — profile ID exists in EVO OLA leads, and neither the email nor the profile ID is also held as a CAS profile.
    • SNP — email exists in EVO SNP marketing communications.
    • Direct ingestion (Ambassador, One to One) — email does not exist under any other source system.
  3. 3Combine the four groups and remove duplicates.
  4. 4Remove the market's list of known excluded accounts (maintained per market in the notebook).
  5. 5Flag a profile as a test profile if any of the email, name or acquisition-source rules below match.
  6. 6Add the three Y/N indicator columns (name contains "test", JTI account, inbucket user).
  7. 7Count the distinct flagged profiles → KPI value. The result is written per market and report month, replacing any earlier run for the same period.
Email matching is case-insensitive. A profile only needs to match one rule to be counted.
MeasureDistinct uuid flagged as test profile
ScopeL1 profiles still present in EVO (CAS, OLA, SNP) plus direct-ingestion-only profiles
UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Primary DBdb_l1_harmonization_[mkt].profile
Supporting SourceEVO extracts: CAS consumers, OLA leads, SNP marketing communications
Outputtest_profiles_kpi (partitioned by market, report_month)
Key Fields
profile.id_profile profile.email profile.first_name profile.last_name profile.legacy_system profile.acquisition_source profile.date_created_ts

Test Detection Rules

A profile is flagged if it matches at least one rule. [mkt] is the market code (e.g. es, lt, jo).

Rule group What is flagged
Email — test keywords Starts with "test"; contains test around a "+" or after "@"; contains testtesttest, ploomtest, testploom, olatest, test123, devtest, deraftest, .tester, dummy, delete, sample@, prod_1 or "example" in the domain
Email — anonymised Contains anonym, anonymised or anonymized
Email — market patterns Market code combined with test, ploom, device or prod — e.g. [mkt]…test, [mkt]_test, +[mkt]_lead_test, [mkt]…ploom, [mkt]…device…test, [mkt]…prod, …ploom…[mkt], prod…[mkt]
Email — internal & test domains @jti.com, @accenture.com, @intellias.com, @globant.com, @fifty-five.com, @monogo.pl, @inbucket-smtp.jtides.com, testinator, @mailinator.com, @yopmail, @fivermail.com, @example.com, @simplelogin.com, @duck.com, @lastname1.com, @lastname2.com, @blackandwitheteam., marketing@gmail.com
Name rules First or last name contains "test" or "deleted"; name is exactly a placeholder (test, synthetic*, anonymised, anonymized, name, ffsdfsd); both names are a single letter or digit; name is only digits; name is one letter repeated (e.g. "aaa")
* "synthetic" applies to first name only
Acquisition source Acquisition source contains "test"
Excluded before flagging Known accounts listed per market in the notebook (currently maintained for CH, DE, JO, LT, LV, ME, PL, PT, RS) are removed before the rules are applied
Prepared for the JTI Profile Cleansing KPI Project  •  Version 1.1

Orphan Profiles

CDP records that have no matching consumer or lead record in EVO — indicating the profile was created through a route outside the standard data pipeline and is not traceable to a known source.

UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Primary Databasedb_l1_harmonization_[mkt]
Supporting Databasedb_temp_dq_[mkt]

What the query does

Performs an anti-join between CDP profiles and EVO records (CAS consumers + OLA leads + SNPs). Any CDP record with no match in any of the three EVO tables is classified as an orphan profile.

Result fields

  • profile.id_profile
  • profile.email
  • profile.legacy_system
  • profile.date_created_timestamp
  • evo_ola_leads.uuid
  • evo_cas_consumers.uuid
  • evo_snp
Formula: Absolute count of CDP profiles with no EVO match
  1. 1Load all CDP profiles from db_l1_harmonization_[mkt].
  2. 2Perform anti-join against EVO CAS consumers (evo_cas_consumers) using UUID / legacy_system linkage.
  3. 3From the unmatched set, perform a second anti-join against EVO OLA leads (evo_ola_leads).
  4. 4From the remaining set, perform a third anti-join against EVO SNPs (evo_snp).
  5. 5Profiles with no match in any of the three EVO tables → KPI value (orphan count).
  6. 6Result is reported as an absolute count (not a percentage) — tracking the number of orphan profiles that need remediation.
Orphans may include profiles created via direct ingestion routes that bypass EVO. The date_created_timestamp helps triage recently created orphans.
MeasureOrphan profile count (no EVO match)
ScopeAll CDP profiles (profile.id_profile)
UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Primary DBdb_l1_harmonization_[mkt]
Supporting DBdb_temp_dq_[mkt]
Key Fields
profile.id_profile profile.email profile.legacy_system profile.date_created_timestamp evo_ola_leads.uuid evo_cas_consumers.uuid evo_snp

Consent Integration

Measures the gap between consent records held in OneTrust and those successfully harmonized into CDP — a key compliance and data completeness indicator.

UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Source Databasedb_temp_dq_[mkt]
Target Databasedb_stg_harmonization_[mkt]

What the query does

Compares OneTrust consent records against CDP consents for each approved consent purpose across all markets. Mismatches — consents present in OneTrust but absent or incorrect in CDP — are flagged as the integration gap.

Result fields

  • market_code
  • purpose
  • onetrust_status
  • consent_type
  • consent_status
  • email
Formula: Count of OneTrust consents absent or mismatched in CDP
  1. 1Load consent records from OneTrust source (db_temp_dq_[mkt].onetrust_source_consent) filtered to approved consent purposes per market.
  2. 2Load harmonized CDP consent records from db_stg_harmonization_[mkt].onetrust_consents.
  3. 3For each email + purpose combination, compare OneTrust status against CDP consent status.
  4. 4Records present in OneTrust but absent or with a mismatched status in CDP are flagged as the integration gap.
  5. 5Count the flagged records → KPI value, reported as an absolute gap count per market and purpose.
Some markets use purpose name variants (e.g. marketing_sms, allchannels) — market-specific purpose names must be validated before running.
MeasureConsent records missing or mismatched in CDP (gap count)
ScopeConsent records in OneTrust for approved purposes
UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Source DBdb_temp_dq_[mkt].onetrust_source_consent
Target DBdb_stg_harmonization_[mkt].onetrust_consents
Key Fields
market_code purpose onetrust_status consent_type consent_status

Profile Contactability

The percentage of profiles that are contactable — having either a valid phone + SMS consent, or a valid email + email consent — including orphan and direct ingestion profiles to show the full impact of cleansing.

UnitPercentage
FrequencyMonthly
Primary Databasedb_l2_unification_[mkt]
Technical Databasedb_technical_[mkt]

What the query does

Calculates the share of profiles satisfying at least one contactability condition — (valid phone AND SMS consent) OR (valid email AND email consent). Orphan profiles and direct ingestion profiles are included in the denominator to give a true picture of the cleansing impact on reachable audience.

Result fields

  • profile.id_profile
  • profile.phone
  • profile.email
  • consents.desc_consent
  • consents.consent_status
  • phone_validity.is_contactable
  • email_validity.is_contactable
Formula: (Contactable Profiles ÷ All Profiles incl. Orphan + DI) × 100
  1. 1Load all profiles from db_l2_unification_[mkt] including orphan and direct-ingestion (DI) profiles.
  2. 2For each profile, evaluate Condition A: phone_validity.is_contactable = true AND SMS consent is active (consents.consent_status = 'active' for SMS purpose).
  3. 3Evaluate Condition B: email_validity.is_contactable = true AND email consent is active for email purpose.
  4. 4Profiles satisfying Condition A OR Condition B → Numerator.
  5. 5All profiles (including orphan + DI) → Denominator. Compute: (Numerator ÷ Denominator) × 100.
Phone validity rules are sourced from db_technical_[mkt]. Including orphan and DI profiles in the denominator shows the true potential audience gain from cleansing.
NumeratorProfiles meeting at least one contactability condition
DenominatorAll profiles incl. orphan + direct ingestion profiles
UnitPercentage
FrequencyMonthly
Primary DBdb_l2_unification_[mkt]
Technical DBdb_technical_[mkt]
Key Fields
profile.id_profile profile.phone profile.email consents.desc_consent consents.consent_status phone_validity.is_contactable email_validity.is_contactable
Prepared for the JTI Profile Cleansing KPI Project  •  Version 1.1

Profile Contactability GDM

The percentage of active (non-deactivated) CDP profiles that can be contacted — valid email with an active marketing email consent, or valid phone with an active marketing SMS consent. Reported twice: before the market's GDM cut-off date and on the fully migrated estate. Also in Old GDM, re-built on the New GDM.

UnitPercentage
FrequencyMonthly
Primary Databasedb_l2_segmentation_[mkt]
Data LayerL2 Segmentation + Technical

What the query does

Builds two profile sets from the CDP L2 segmentation profile table (excluding deactivated accounts): profiles created before the market's GDM cut-off date, and all profiles. For each set it counts profiles that are contactable through a valid channel with an active marketing consent, and divides by the set size.

Result fields

  • contactable_profiles_before_migration
  • total_profiles_before_migration
  • percentage_of_contactable_profiles_before_migration
  • contactable_profiles_full_migration
  • total_profiles_full_migration
  • percentage_of_contactable_profiles_full_migration
  • market
Formula: (Contactable Profiles ÷ Total Active Profiles) × 100 — calculated Before Migration and Full Migration
  1. 1The Before Migration set requires created_date_ts < the market's GDM cut-off date.
  2. 2Join db_technical_[mkt].email_validity on trimmed, lower-case email and db_technical_[mkt].phone_validity on mobile.
  3. 3Join db_l2_segmentation_[mkt].consents on cdp_profile_id. For Before Migration, only consents updated before the cut-off date are used.
  4. 4A profile is contactable when (email is_contactable = 1 AND [mkt]_ploom_marketing_email is ACTIVE) OR (phone is_contactable = 1 AND [mkt]_ploom_marketing_sms is ACTIVE). Count distinct cdp_profile_id → Numerator.
  5. 5Count all profiles in the set → Denominator. Compute (Numerator ÷ Denominator) × 100, rounded to 2 decimals (division by zero returns null).
The cut-off date is market-specific (e.g. JO = 27 Oct 2026). Comparing the two percentages shows the impact of the GDM migration on contactable audience.
NumeratorContactable active profiles (distinct cdp_profile_id)
DenominatorActive profiles in the set
UnitPercentage
FrequencyMonthly
Primary DBdb_l2_segmentation_[mkt]
Data LayerL2 Segmentation + Technical
Cut-offMarket GDM cut-off date
Source Tables
db_l2_segmentation_[mkt].profile db_l2_segmentation_[mkt].consents db_technical_[mkt].email_validity db_technical_[mkt].phone_validity
Key Fields
cdp_profile_id email mobile created_date_ts consent_desc consent_status updated_date_ts is_contactable

Orphan Profiles GDM

CDP L2 segmentation profiles that have no matching consumer, lead or incumbent record in EVO, or that were anonymised in EVO but still exist in CDP. Also in Old GDM, re-built on the New GDM.

UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Primary Databasedb_l2_segmentation_[mkt]
Data LayerL2 Segmentation + Temp DQ

What the query does

Builds the full EVO dataset (CAS consumers, OLA leads not already in CAS, and incumbent profiles) and compares it with CDP L2 profiles by UUID. Profiles missing from EVO, or anonymised in EVO but still live in CDP, are returned as orphans with a comment explaining why.

Result fields

  • des_profile_uuid
  • cdp_email
  • first_name
  • last_name
  • source_system_name
  • created_date_ts
  • evo_email
  • Comment
Formula: Orphan Profile Count = COUNT(DISTINCT des_profile_uuid) across both orphan types
  1. 1Build the EVO dataset: evo_cas_consumers ∪ evo_ola_leads (only UUIDs not already in CAS) ∪ evo_incumbent_profiles (only UUIDs not already in EVO CAS and EVO OLA).
  2. 2Type A — Profile not present in EVO: CDP profiles in db_l2_segmentation_[mkt].profile whose des_profile_uuid is not in the EVO dataset.
  3. 3Type B — Anonymised in EVO and present in CDP: CDP profiles matched to EVO by UUID where the EVO email contains anonym.
  4. 4Keep records where the CDP email differs from the EVO email (trimmed, lower-case) or the EVO email is missing.
  5. 5Keep profiles created before the reporting cut-off timestamp, then de-duplicate → orphan list. Count distinct des_profile_uuid → KPI value.
The orphan list is the action list for cleansing: Type A profiles are removed from CDP; Type B profiles must be anonymised in CDP to match EVO.
MeasureDistinct orphan profiles (des_profile_uuid)
Orphan typesNot present in EVO · Anonymised in EVO, present in CDP
UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Primary DBdb_l2_segmentation_[mkt]
Data LayerL2 Segmentation + Temp DQ
Source Tables
db_l2_segmentation_[mkt].profile db_temp_dq_[mkt].evo_cas_consumers db_temp_dq_[mkt].evo_ola_leads db_temp_dq_[mkt].evo_incumbent_profiles

3 Systems Consent Integration

Every OneTrust consent (email + purpose) is checked against EVO and CDP. Consents missing in one or both systems are classified and flagged for orphan status. New KPI introduced with the New GDM.

UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Primary Databasedb_temp_dq_[mkt]
Data LayerTemp DQ + L2 Segmentation

What the query does

Uses OneTrust as the driving set and left-joins the latest EVO consent and the CDP consent for the same email and purpose. Each gap is classified by which system is missing it, and enriched with EVO presence and CDP profile flags. Consents present in all three systems are excluded.

Result fields

  • email
  • purpose
  • ot_status
  • ot_last_transaction
  • evo_status
  • evo_last_transaction
  • cdp_status
  • cdp_last_transaction
  • observation
  • present_in_evo_consumers
  • present_in_evo_leads
  • present_in_evo_incumbent
  • is_orphan
  • present_in_cdp_l2_segmentation_profile
  • cdp_profile_id
Formula: Consent Gap Count = OneTrust consents (email + purpose) not present in both EVO and CDP
  1. 1OneTrust base: consents from onetrust_source_consent for the migrated markets' purposes, with last_transaction older than 2 days (allows for sync lag).
  2. 2EVO: latest row per email + purpose from evo_soruce_consent (purpose name normalised; ranked by last transaction date, then updated/created/synced time).
  3. 3CDP: consents from db_l2_segmentation_[mkt].consents joined to profile to get the email.
  4. 4Left-join EVO and CDP to OneTrust on email + purpose and set the observation: present in all systems · only in OneTrust · in OneTrust and EVO but missing in CDP · in OneTrust and CDP but missing in EVO. Consents present in all systems are not counted.
  5. 5Add flags: presence in EVO consumers / leads / incumbent, is_orphan (in none of them) and presence in the CDP L2 profile table.
The 2-day buffer on OneTrust transactions avoids flagging consents that are still syncing to EVO and CDP.
MeasureOneTrust consents missing in EVO and/or CDP

Consent Status Mismatch GDM

3 Systems Consent Status Mismatch compares consent statuses across OneTrust, EVO and CDP. It highlights consents whose status is not the same in all 3 systems. Consents with the same status in all 3 systems are in sync and are not counted. New KPI introduced with the New GDM.

UnitCount
FrequencyMonthly
Primary Databasedb_temp_dq_[mkt]
Data LayerTemp DQ + L2 Segmentation

What the query does

Lines up each consent (email + purpose) in OneTrust, EVO and CDP and compares the three statuses — Active, Withdrawn, Not given, Opt-out, etc. A consent is counted as a mismatch when any two systems disagree: OneTrust vs EVO, OneTrust vs CDP, or EVO vs CDP. Each row is enriched with a test-email flag and EVO / L2 presence flags.

Result fields

  • email
  • purpose
  • onetrust_status
  • evo_status
  • cdp_status
  • onetrust_last_transaction
  • evo_last_transaction
  • cdp_last_transaction
  • test_emails
  • present_in_evo_cas
  • present_in_evo_ola
  • present_in_evo_incumbent
  • present_in_L2_profile_table
  • is_orphan
Formula: Status Mismatch Count = consents (email + purpose) whose status is not identical in OneTrust, EVO and CDP
  1. 1OneTrust: consents from onetrust_source_consent for the migrated markets' purposes.
  2. 2EVO: latest consent per email + purpose from evo_soruce_consent.
  3. 3CDP: consents from db_l2_segmentation_[mkt].consents, joined to profile for the email.
  4. 4Match the three sources on email (lower-case, special characters stripped) and purpose, then compare statuses case-insensitively: OneTrust vs EVO, OneTrust vs CDP and EVO vs CDP. If any pair differs the consent is a mismatch; if all 3 agree it is in sync and not counted.
  5. 5Add flags: test_emails (known test / dummy / internal domain patterns), presence in evo_cas_consumers, evo_ola_leads, evo_incumbent and db_l2_unification_[mkt].profile. Keep profiles present in EVO CAS or OLA and OneTrust transactions older than 2 days. Count rows → KPI value.
'Not given' is a valid status and is compared like any other — e.g. Not given in OneTrust but Active in EVO and CDP is a mismatch. Test emails are flagged, not removed, so they can be reviewed separately.

Implementation Notes

  • Use the latest market-specific values from the KPI SQL queries wherever the query references specific market codes and purpose names.
  • For invalid phone validation, confirm the country code prefix, phone length without prefix, and total length for each market before finalising the rule table.
  • For the consent KPI, validate market-specific purpose names — some markets use slightly different consent labels such as marketing_phone, marketing_sms, or allchannels.
  • Each KPI is built using a canonical market list so every market appears in output even when the gap count is zero — ensuring no market is silently omitted.
  • For Profile Contactability (Old GDM KPI 3), the denominator includes orphan and direct ingestion profiles to give the full picture of what cleansing would unlock in terms of contactable audience.
Reminder — database naming convention All databases follow the pattern [db_name]_[market_code] (e.g., db_l1_harmonization_de). Market codes must match exactly as listed in the Market Codes reference.
